canada.title: Ravi Kahlon focusing on family, but won't rule out B.C. NDP leadership run
canada.summary: Former B.C. New Democrat housing minister Ravi Kahlon says his priority is his family after opting not to run in the snap election that toppled his party's government — but he is not closing the door on politics.

canada.title: Death of man, 22, in Pelican Narrows considered suspicious: Sask RCMP
canada.summary: RCMP received a report of an injured man at a home in Pelican Narrows on Thursday around 7 p.m. Police said the seriously injured man was taken to hospital, where he later died.

canada.title: Suspect identified in Toronto home invasion where residents were shot, attacked with hammer
canada.summary: Daijohn Richards, 23, of Toronto has been identified as a suspect wanted in connection with the Bridle Path neighbourhood home invasion investigation, where a family of four was shot at and attacked with a hammer.

canada.title: Cold Lake pushes for provincewide ride-hailing regulations
canada.summary: The City of Cold Lake is looking to advocate for provincial regulations that would make it easier for services like Uber and Lyft to operate in different jurisdictions.

canada.title: Man dies after fight in Montreal’s Rosemont-La Petite-Patrie
canada.summary: Montreal police say two men arrested on Friday in connection with the death of a 20-year-old man are facing murder-related charges.

canada.title: Why Toronto’s municipal election turnout beat the provincial average
canada.summary: Unofficial results collected by the Association of Municipalities of Ontario show 46 per cent of those eligible to vote in Toronto did so in this week's municipal election.

canada.title: North Atlantic right whale spotted entangled in gear
canada.summary: Fisheries and Oceans Canada says a surveillance flight spotted the whale on Oct. 21 between New Brunswick's Acadian Peninsula, P.E.I. and Quebec's Îles-de-la-Madeleine.

canada.title: Alberta’s clocks won’t fall back this weekend. Here’s how that might impact your daily life
canada.summary: After years of grumbling about the biannual time change, Albertans will get their first taste this weekend of what it’s like to keep clocks the same year-round. Here’s a look at what will change and what won’t.

canada.title: Number of unqualified Nunavut teachers nearly doubled in 5 years
canada.summary: The number of teachers who have letters of authority in Nunavut classrooms has nearly doubled in 5 years, from around 50 to now over 90. Nunavut's education minister David Akeeagok says he's not concerned about the increase, but the teachers’ union warns of the growing reliance on unqualified teachers.

canada.title: Montreal police officer allegedly deleted domestic violence evidence from victim's phone
canada.summary: According to Radio-Canada, a Montreal police officer at Station 39 allegedly deleted video evidence provided in 2025 by a woman who was a victim of domestic violence.

canada.title: Drug runner? Arms dealer? The Adeline-C made waves in Halifax and beyond
canada.summary: The Adeline-C arrived in Halifax on Oct. 31, 1981, filled with state-of-the-art equipment, but it was soon abandoned by its crew. It would be years before its role in a complex U.S. drug smuggling operation worth as much as $200 million US became fully known.

canada.title: B.C. won't be changing its clocks on Nov. 1. Here's what you need to know
canada.summary: For the first time in decades, British Columbians won't have to change their clocks on Nov. 1 like much of the rest of the U.S. and Canada. Here's what technology experts are advising British Columbians to do both ahead of, and after, time changes go into effect elsewhere.

canada.title: Sask. musician's terminal brain cancer diagnosis prompts outpouring of support
canada.summary: Julie Atter had a bright and varied career as a musician and as a band instructor. The Regina woman worked tirelessly to promote music and help support kids in their music education. After a diagnosis of terminal brain cancer, fellow music lovers have launched initiatives in her honour, including the Julie Atter Pay It Forward fund and a song inspired by her.

canada.title: Silver screen returns to Selkirk with reopening of Garry Theatre
canada.summary: The nearly 78-year-old Garry Theatre has reopened in Selkirk, after closing its doors in 2021, when Landmark Cinemas listed the property for sale.

canada.title: I'm a millennial mom who hates Halloween — but I give it my all for the sake of the kids
canada.summary: Abigail Matula didn't love Halloween as a kid. Now, she writes, she hates it.

canada.title: New equipment makes Whitehorse hospital lab ‘most modern’ in the North, says health minister
canada.summary: New chemical analyzers at the Whitehorse General Hospital mean faster, more reliable test results. The upgrades are part of a $3-million plan to modernize the hospital’s medical laboratory.

canada.title: Attacks on women in politics far more personal than those aimed at men, expert says
canada.summary: A New Brunswick mayor says online abuse of politicians can spill into real life, while an international expert says personal attacks on politicians who are women are pushing some out of politics and keeping others from running.

canada.title: How witchcraft lore encouraged kindness among neighbours in Newfoundland and Labrador
canada.summary: Isolated in small communities with limited resources, rural Newfoundlanders and Labradorians had to rely on each other to survive. Thinking someone could bewitch you if you mistreated them was a reason to help all your neighbours, even the ones you didn’t particularly like.
